extracted.intended_audience: community college faculty, staff, and campus grant-writers (educational institutions seeking external funding)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical manual for developing, researching, and writing grant proposals for campuses (especially two-year/community colleges), covering identifying funders, structuring proposals, and completing all proposal components and packaging. Includes section-by-section guidance and sample components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of public funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes characteristics of public funding sources (federal, state, and local governments) and provides information on sources and methods for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies how public funders operate and where to look for opportunities; compares federal, state, and local funding approaches and submission requirements (as presented in the manual's first section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of private funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes characteristics of private funding sources (foundations, corporations or businesses, civic groups, and individuals) and provides information on sources and methods for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains differences among foundations, corporate giving, civic groups, and individual donors and provides methods for researching and approaching each type of private funder (as summarized in the manual).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of grants and proposals; overview and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction to proposal writing focusing on the different types of grants, types of proposals, an overview of the entire process, and options for the style and tone of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps writers choose appropriate proposal type and adopt an appropriate style/tone; provides an end-to-end process overview to guide planning and sequencing of proposal tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizing the proposal: developing ideas and program design
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions on organizing the proposal, focusing on developing ideas for the grant and developing the program design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on turning program ideas into coherent design and structure for the proposal; includes advice on organization and logical flow of program components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of a proposal or inquiry letter
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of the components required in a full proposal or in an inquiry letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines what belongs in brief inquiries versus full proposals and what core elements funders expect in either submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction and organizational capability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth guidance for crafting the proposal introduction and an organizational capability statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to present the organization, its mission, capacity, and credibility to assure funders that the applicant can carry out the proposed work (presented section-by-section in the manual).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of need
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth guidance on writing the statement of need for the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how to justify the project by documenting the problem or need with evidence and convincing argumentation tailored to funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth guidance on defining the project's goals and measurable objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers writing clear, realistic goals and specific, measurable objectives that align with the statement of need and proposed methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth guidance on describing the project methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to present planned activities, timeline, staffing, and methods so reviewers can assess feasibility and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on addressing future funding within the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to discuss sustainability, plans for continuing the project beyond the grant period, and strategies for securing additional funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth guidance on the evaluation component of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how to propose appropriate evaluation measures, data collection, and assessment strategies to show how project success will be measured and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: sources of income and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed discussion of the budget, including sources of income and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers constructing a realistic budget listing all income sources and cost categories so funders can judge fiscal soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget narrative accompanying the actual budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on writing the budget narrative that accompanies the numerical budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to justify budget line items, clarify assumptions, and link costs to project activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the grant proposal: packaging and submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps and components involved in completing the grant proposal, including the cover letter, title page, table of contents, summary, forms, attachments, editing, and packaging the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides checklists and procedures for finalizing submission materials, ensuring required forms and attachments are included, and presenting a polished package to funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appendices: samples and editing checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices provide a list of major foundations, sample proposal components, and an editing checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises using provided sample components as models and following the editing checklist to improve clarity, formatting, and compliance with funder instructions.
